title: Teluni Initial Release Requirements and Acceptance
html:
Project documentation · Approved release policies · Acceptance targets · Product architecture

Scope and acceptance rules

Decided: complete the company-to-screen journey with tenant-safe remote management, images/videos, configurable data catalogs, freeform simultaneous content, regional schedules, offline Android TV playback and monitoring. The owner prioritizes intended product capability/quality over reducing scope solely to fit an MVP label. The historical mvp.md path remains the stable requirements entry point.

Every capability below is a requirement, not implemented functionality. The plan owns delivery status; release policies own business behavior and the questionnaire decision record; acceptance targets own numeric limits and qualification goals. PH-09 policy/target selection is complete as of 2026-10-18. No hardware, pilot or performance qualification is inferred.

ID Functional requirement Required acceptance evidence before release
FR-01 Companies, branches, users, company settings, public company signup/automatic activation, authentication, scoped standard/custom profiles and temporary access Two synthetic companies each have branches/users. Authorized members manage allowed resources; direct API attempts, lists/search, media/catalog access and identifier substitution cannot cross company/branch scope. Verify responsible-administrator approval, trusted account linking, strong/recent authentication, recovery, session bounds and 30-second revocation using IA-01–IA-16. Public activation must satisfy commercial/privacy/abuse gates; platform operation has no implicit customer-content access.
FR-02 Device identity, temporary-code pairing, company/branch assignment, name/configuration and safe unlink An authorized user claims a displayed code once. Expired/replayed codes, concurrent claims, wrong-scope assignment and revoked identities fail safely. Reassignment requires verified cleanup/reset and cannot expose previous tenant data/credentials; unreachable erasure is shown as pending.
FR-03 Supported horizontal/vertical orientation Qualified devices display supported orientations correctly; invalid geometry or unsupported profiles have explicit outcomes rather than silent support claims.
FR-04 Private image/video upload, validation, organization, metadata, reuse, conversion and reference-aware deletion Approved profiles upload, validate/convert and play on tested hardware. Spoofed type, malformed/oversized content and unauthorized reads fail safely. Archive/deletion/retention preserve protected draft, active, staging and recovery references; assisted draft changes need confirmation.
FR-05 Playlists, ordered items, configurable image duration, full-video playback, looping, device/group assignment and qualified cuts/fades Deterministic order and preview/player duration agreement. Devices have zero or one company-owned group, including cross-branch groups; explicit individual programming replaces the whole group source. Confirmed source changes use published content or an intentionally empty destination. Ordinary item completion and coordinated-page timing follow release policies.
FR-06 Dates, local hours, weekdays, overnight recurrence, regional schedules and deterministic conflict/no-match rules Shared backend/player fixtures cover inclusive starts/exclusive ends, final-date clipping, all-day/equal-time validation, timezone/DST, overlapping same-output windows, regional exceptions and empty windows. Optional defaults otherwise give safe neutral output; expired commercial content is not an implicit fallback.
FR-07 Preview, publication, immutable consistent versions, desired/downloaded/active state and last-valid preservation Ordinary drafts do not affect screens. Authorized price saves automatically publish affected published bindings through durable/retry-safe intent, excluding unrelated drafts. Concurrent/repeated operations and unknown outcomes are reconcilable. Complete supported versions activate only after validated staging; failures never replace valid state with mixed/corrupt resources.
FR-08 Android TV playback, bounded offline operation and controlled recovery/update Qualified devices play local media/catalog snapshots without normal backend streaming, through the selected offline/clock/authorization envelope, reboot, power interruption and protocol/update cases in playback acceptance. Expired authorization or untrusted time has an explicit safe outcome.
FR-09 Scoped connection/last-contact/app/storage/sync/playback diagnostics Show observed timestamps, stale/offline thresholds and actual version states. Distinguish failed sync, regional rendering failure and lost contact from stopped playback. Reconnection reconciles state without leaking data or claiming unseen erasure.
FR-10 Freeform simultaneous composition, independent areas with optional coordinated pages, per-area schedules, multiple videos and configurable mixed audio Users position/resize areas and preview copy/import/export of versioned textual layouts. An active regional schedule survives a global page change; coordinated areas follow the selected page timeline. Isolated area failure/no-match preserves unaffected geometry/output. Qualified rendering/audio profiles and pagination remain readable and work offline.
FR-11 User-defined typed catalogs, fields and records with layout bindings, including products/prices and weekly agendas Users configure a non-product catalog as well as a product configuration. Validate schema/version evolution, scoped record/media references, branch price overrides and import boundaries. Data-driven views paginate without silent name/price clipping. Price publication/expiry and unavailable-item defaults work from consistent offline snapshots; customization cannot execute arbitrary code or cross tenant boundaries.

Managed campaigns remain future scope; scheduled content and published price-validity rules provide the initial promotion behavior without approving a separate campaign engine.

Approved PH-09 decisions

The canonical release policies retain the earlier assignment/group/default/pairing directions and consolidate questionnaire P01–P31. The decision record distinguishes direct owner answers from the ten explicitly delegated selections. It records the custom-catalog expansion, hybrid area model and automatic price-publication exception rather than retaining obsolete mandatory coordinated progression or a product-only schema.

The numeric values, measurement boundaries and FR/NF mapping are in release acceptance targets. Target approval is distinct from a test result, supported-device promise or commercial SLA. Use those sources when implementing contracts/tests; do not infer policy from the old temporary questionnaire's unfilled optional summary table.

Proposed behavior requiring confirmation

PH-09 has no outstanding owner questionnaire answer. Remaining work concerns technical review and other human actions: physical tenant enforcement; actual Keycloak compatibility, session/assurance integration and scoped authorization verification (PJ-24; PH-11 decision selection and the identity/access matrix are completed); external identity/Google/mail setup (PH-15–PH-17); manifest/layout/catalog schema, renderers, persistence, processing and credential/trusted-time mechanisms (PJ-07/D-01–D-11); real hardware qualification (PH-08); infrastructure/restore evidence (PH-10); and privacy/commercial review (PH-12/PH-13). The owner accepted ADR-0018–ADR-0021/ADR-0023–ADR-0025 on 2026-10-18; any significant new unresolved mechanism still uses the ADR process; approved product policies are not proof that these mechanisms exist.

Nonfunctional requirements

ID Requirement and acceptance boundary Measurement / remaining work
NF-01 Server-side tenant/branch isolation and least privilege across stored/derived data, including custom fields/catalogs, private media and bulk operations Allow/deny and adversarial reference tests; reviewed D-01/D-02. Device offline authorization AT-15 does not grant cross-tenant access.
NF-02 Complete offline activation, integrity, bounded retries, storage reserve, interruption/startup/clock recovery AT-01–AT-20 and shared failure fixtures; actual hardware/mechanisms remain D-03/D-04/D-07 and PH-08.
NF-03 Measured API/panel response, bounded work/pagination, file-processing/transfer and fleet behavior AT-11/AT-14/AT-21–AT-23; record real media/network/host measurements separately. PH-10 remains open.
NF-04 Environment configuration, durable external media, rehearsed backup/restore and host migration RPO/RTO, destination/retention and residential availability remain PH-10, with PH-13 privacy/retention review.
NF-05 Structured redacted diagnostics and attributable audit for security, publication/prices and device lifecycle AT-14/AT-20/AT-24 plus reviewed audit integrity/retention under D-09/PH-13. Operational report retention does not decide legal/security audit retention.
NF-06 Localizable web/player, initially pt-BR/en-US, explicit locale/timezone and exact currency semantics Local schedule/DST/clock fixtures and generic date/time/money field rendering; D-10 selects exact representation/libraries before contracts.
NF-07 Nontechnical core workflows, keyboard/responsive interaction and accessibility AT-23/AT-25; observed tasks and automated/manual web checks. Scans alone do not certify accessibility.
NF-08 Backend/player protocol overlap, controlled updates, preserved compatible playback and tested rollback AT-26 and D-04/D-07 support matrix; version numbers/store/installer remain technical work.
NF-09 Measure storage, traffic, processing, hardware/support cost without mandatory paid dependencies AT-21 reference load, processing/media measurements and PH-12 commercial envelope; no unlimited-resource or revenue claim.

Release acceptance journey

  1. Establish two synthetic companies through verified enrollment with responsible administrators, differently scoped branches/operators and qualified Android TV devices. Exercise IA-01–IA-16 login/linking/recovery/session/revocation/approval/support cases and API/media/catalog allow/deny boundaries; no implicit platform content privilege.
  2. Pair devices, create a cross-branch group and an explicit individual exception. Upload media; configure a custom weekly-agenda catalog and product/price configuration. Compose independent and coordinated areas, regional schedules and an optional default; preview and publish A.
  3. Verify local multi-video/audio/catalog rendering under the qualified profile. Edit drafts without changing A. Save a price and verify automatic consistent publication from published dependencies without leaking unrelated drafts; test concurrent edits, duplicate delivery and failed/unknown outcomes.
  4. Publish B while playback continues. Cut network/power at download/staging/activation boundaries and verify complete valid A or B. Isolate a runtime regional fault without confusing it with incomplete-generation activation. Check protected references and insufficient disk outcomes.
  5. Exercise schedule/date/DST/promotion/no-match/pagination and regional-page timing offline. Test the trusted-clock and authorization deadlines, restart/recovery and the expected safe neutral states.
  6. Reconnect and reconcile observed state. Unlink/revoke while offline, then verify cleanup before cross-company pairing. Exercise historical recovery without expired offers or resurrected credentials and validate controlled protocol/app updates.
  7. Rehearse database-plus-media restore and endpoint migration in isolation. Record target-linked load/usability/hardware evidence, costs and residual risk before real-customer acceptance.

Evidence includes automated contract/security/integration/browser tests, representative hardware/power/network tests, restore results and user observation. Delivery can be incremental; an operational release requires the complete applicable acceptance set. Passing foundation validation only checks currently implemented foundation/docs.

Explicitly outside the MVP

The historical heading remains a stable route; initial scope now includes freeform composition, configurable catalogs and their approved commercial defaults. Further unreviewed widgets, managed campaigns, external ERP/POS/partner integration APIs/webhooks/imports, automated billing/subscriptions, white-label, AI, playback analytics, general remote-control tools, impersonation, synchronization across separate screens and alternative players remain future unless independently approved. PH-11 separately selects scoped consent-based human support, custom access profiles and optional independent publication approvals for the initial release; these policies remain unimplemented. Generic fields do not approve arbitrary executable plugins, unrestricted data collection or all roadmap capabilities.
